Welcome to SamirGeoConvert Pro

A complete surveying toolkit for Saudi Arabia and Egypt: coordinate & datum conversion on the official SANSRS parameters, plate-motion epochs, geoid heights, COGO, QC, CAD/GIS files, RINEX and technical reports — all offline in your browser.

KSA-GRF17 Epoch Transformation (Arabian Plate Motion)

KSA-GRF17 is fixed at epoch 2017.0, while ITRF2014 / WGS84 coordinates from global services (PPP, IGS, CSRS, AUSPOS) move with the Arabian plate (~4–5 cm/year). This tool applies the official time-dependent transformation EPSG:9334 (rotation rates −1.199, +0.107, −1.468 mas/yr).

Use this for PPP / IGS / AUSPOS results in ITRF at the observation epoch. RTK on KSA-CORS already delivers KSA-GRF17 — do not apply it twice. The GRF-TT portal uses the static EPSG:9383 set (Point Converter).

Batch epoch transformation

File columns: ID, Lat, Lon, h (geographic, decimal degrees). Uses the epoch and direction above.

Orthometric Height (H = h − N)

Enter a point in any system with its ellipsoidal height. The undulation N comes from a loaded geoid model, the built-in Arabia Geoid, or a value you type (e.g. from the GASGI portal).

Step 1: load points (ID, X, Y, h). Step 2: N is computed from every available model; you can also import N columns from the GASGI portal or GeoidEval. Step 3: export H for each model and the differences between models.

Geoid Models

Load any geoid grid you own (e.g. KSA-GEOID21 from GEOSA, EGM2008 regional cut). Supported: NOAA .gtx, GRAVSOFT .gra/.gri, Surfer ASCII .grd (DSAA), ISG .isg and XYZ text (lat lon N). Loaded models are stored in this browser.

Grid ⇄ Ground

Compute the combined scale factor automatically from the project location and mean height (grid scale × elevation factor), or type your own factor. Ground coordinates are scaled about a chosen origin.

Projection used for the grid

Local Calibration (2-D Helmert / 4-parameter)

Fit a conformal transformation between two coordinate sets using common control points (e.g. GNSS grid → local site grid). Residuals and RMS are shown; then apply it to any other points.

Quantities & Volumes

Points of the ground (ID E N Z) are triangulated (TIN) and compared with a design level. Gives cut, fill, net volume and areas — for site levelling, excavation and stockpiles.

…or drop a points file (ID E N Z)

Original ground and final surface survey (ID E N Z each). The final surface is triangulated and the original surface is interpolated at a regular grid — volumes are the difference (grid method).

Surface 1 — original ground
…or drop file
Surface 2 — final / design
…or drop file

Road / channel quantities by the average end area method. One section per line: "chainage cut_area fill_area" (m, m²).

Generate contour lines from survey points (TIN) and export them as a 3-D DXF with major / minor layers.

…or drop a points file (ID E N Z)

Traverse Adjustment (angles & distances)

Field-book entry: one row per station — station name, horizontal angle (clockwise from the previous station to the next), and distance to the next station. The angular misclosure is distributed equally, then the linear misclosure by Bowditch or Transit.

Leveling Book

Enter readings row by row: station, BS, IS, FS and distance (m). Blank = no reading. The book is reduced by Rise & Fall or Height of Instrument, with arithmetic checks, misclosure against the closing benchmark, allowable error and adjustment.

Alignment, Offset & Stakeout

Define a centreline (polyline vertices E N) and its start chainage. Then get station & offset of any points, compute points from station & offset, or check stakeout (design vs as-built).

Offset sign: + right of the centreline (looking forward), − left.

Perpendicular offset of points from the line A–B (or from the centreline above if A/B are empty).

Network Adjustment (Least Squares)

Observed height differences between benchmarks, weighted by line length (σ = mm/√km). Fixed benchmarks hold their heights.

Baseline vectors (ECEF ΔX ΔY ΔZ in metres) with their standard deviations, between stations; fixed stations in ECEF X Y Z (e.g. KSA-CORS). Results are also given in the chosen output system.

Output system

GCP Planning

Load the project boundary (KML / KMZ polygon) or paste E N vertices. GCPs are placed at the corners, along the edges and on an interior grid at your spacing; check points are put where they are farthest from GCPs.

Drop boundary KML / KMZ

Flight Planner (GSD)

Choose the camera, then a target GSD or a flight height. Gives footprint, line & photo spacing, trigger interval and — for an area — lines, images and flight time.

Profiles & Cross Sections from survey points

The survey points (ID E N Z) are triangulated; the long profile and cross sections are sampled along the centreline. Export to Excel and to a DXF drawing (profile + sections with grid).

Point Description Cards

One A4 page per control point: coordinates in KSA-GRF17 (UTM + geographic) and WGS84, ellipsoidal & orthometric height, description, up to 2 photos, a location sketch with nearby points and north arrow, and a Google Maps link. Photos are matched by file name starting with the point ID (e.g. GCP12_1.jpg, GCP12_2.jpg).

Points file system
1) Points file: ID, X, Y, h, [N or H], [description]
2) Photos (multiple, named by point ID)

QC: Compare Two Point Sets

Check-shots vs design, re-observation vs original, or portal vs software. Rows: "ID X1 Y1 [H1] X2 Y2 [H2]" or upload a file. Points beyond the tolerance are flagged.

…or drop a file

Point Statistics (repeat observations)

Paste repeated observations of the same point ("X Y [h]"). Gives mean, standard deviation, RMS about the mean, 2DRMS and the spread — ideal for RTK repeatability checks.

…or drop a file

CAD / GIS File Conversion

Turn a survey points file into a ready AutoCAD drawing: 3-D points, point number / elevation / code labels on separate layers, a layer per feature code, and lines joining points with the same code (line coding).

Points file system
Drawing system (DXF)
File columns: ID, X, Y, Z, Code (code optional). Line coding: codes ending with "ST" start a new line and "END" closes it; otherwise points of the same code are joined in file order. Code "BLD", "BOUNDARY" or ending with "CL" closes the polygon.

Datums & Transformation Parameters

All parameters are stored as Position-Vector (EPSG 9606), datum → WGS84, rotations in arc-seconds and scale in ppm.

Add a custom datum

About SamirGeoConvert Pro

A professional surveying toolkit for Saudi Arabia and Egypt. Everything runs locally in the browser — your coordinates never leave your computer (internet is only used for map tiles and fonts).

Projection mathsKrüger n-series transverse Mercator (6th order), < 1 mm within the zone
GeodesicsVincenty inverse / direct on the selected ellipsoid
Datum transformationExact 3-D 7-parameter Helmert (Position Vector), exact inverse; AGD00 grid for Ain El Abd 1970
KSA-GRF17EPSG:9383 — verified 0.000 m against the GASGI GRF-TT portal
Plate motionEPSG:9334 time-dependent ITRF2014 → KSA-GRF17

Quick guide

  • Point / Batch Converter: any datum and projection to any other, with heights.
  • Heights: built-in Arabia Geoid, your own geoid grids, or values from the GASGI portal — compare models side by side.
  • Survey calculations: inverse, traverse with Bowditch adjustment, area, intersections, grid-ground, local calibration, QC and repeatability statistics.
  • Files: DXF, KML/KMZ, Shapefile and RINEX in bulk.
  • Project: collect points from every tool, map them, save the project file and produce a technical report.
